mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Corporate Registration Certificate of Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Company Registration Office, Supreme Court of Korea (Internet Registration Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: obtain registry certificate, have signature certified by Korean notary where required, then obtain Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. For non-Apostille destinations, use consular legalization by the Korean diplomatic mission and the destination embassy; Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Corporate Registry Extract Confirming Absence of Winding-Up and Liquidation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Company Registration Office, Supreme Court of Korea (Internet Registration Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: registry-issued extract certified and then Apostillized by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular legalization path for non-Hague destinations: registry-issued extract notarized, authenticated by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalized by destination-state embassy or consulate in Seoul. The two paths are mutually exclusive; do not apply both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Resolution of Board of Directors / Power of Attorney appointing formation agent and bank signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors (or manager if no board) of Yuhan Hoesa, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention path: notarized resolution in Korean or English translation, notary certificate attached, then Apostille by Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Non-member-state path: same notarized document, Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then consular legalization at the destination embassy or consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of Yuhan Hoesa (Jeonggwan)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding members and notary public; filed with the District Court Company Registration Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If used abroad, the filed articles are issued as an office-certified copy, then Apostillized by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille member states. For non-member states, use notarization plus Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication plus consular legalization by the destination embassy or consulate. Parallel, exclusive paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for good conduct of intended bank relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Korean bank or foreign bank branch in Korea regulated by the Financial Services Commission under the Banking Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: bank letter notarized by bank officer or notary and Apostillized by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Hague member states. Consular path: notarized bank letter, Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then destination-state consular legalization. No sequential use of Apostille and consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be performed against the consolidated lists published by the United Nations Security Council Sanctions Committee; the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List and non-SDN sanctions lists; the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list; the United Kingdom Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation list; the Republic of Korea domestic Designated Persons list and sanctions measures under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information; and FATF high-risk jurisdictions and call-for-action lists. Compliance protocols require exact and phonetic fuzzy matching of every member, director, manager, assistant, beneficial owner, and counterparty against the foregoing lists, using local Korean name aliases including Hangul, Hanja, and romanized variants, and a minimum 100-point screening algorithm. Any positive PEP or sanctions hit triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, senior management approval, and a suspicious transaction report to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit within the statutory deadline.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Republic of Korea Supreme Court Internet Registry Office (IRO) / District Court Company Registration Section; official name-search module on iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Commercial Act Article 19 requires a company name to be written in Hangul (Korean letters); pure English or romanized words are not accepted as the registered legal name. The registry conducts exact and fuzzy matching under a four-tier convention: (1) identical Hangul name; (2) Hangul homophone or phonetic transliteration equivalence; (3) Hanja and historical Chinese-character corporate-name equivalents; and (4) Romanized aliases and spacing, punctuation, and suffix variants. The legal name must include the company-type indicator similar to Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company); foreign names may be used as a trademark or trade alias but cannot replace the Hangul legal name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant must ask the registry for a written statement of reasons. If the rejection is based on similarity or a prohibited token, the party may amend the proposed name and resubmit for a new search. A substantive refusal may be challenged by filing an appeal with the court having jurisdiction over the registry under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act within 14 days of notice; the petition must identify the legal error, append the original refusal notice, revised articles, evidence of trade-name priority, and any ministerial approval. If the appeal is dismissed, the petitioner may bring an administrative suit, but resubmission with a fresh name is commercially prudent.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, PO Box, or commercial mail forwarder cannot serve as the registered principal office of a Korean Yuhan Hoesa. The registered address must be a physical location where the company keeps essential corporate records and management conducts business. A registered virtual office in a coworking or serviced-office building may be accepted only if the National Tax Service and a bank verify the lease agreement, physical access, and a clearly identified dedicated workspace. For online automotive aftermarket parts retail under ISIC 4791, no special statutory license is required, but Stripe, PayPal, and local bank onboarding will require a verified Korean business address, evidence of rent or ownership, and presence of a local authorized manager. Financial institutions generally reject mailbox-only addresses under the Real Name Financial Transactions requirements and through bank AML policies. If the operation uses third-party logistics and has no inventory, a shared coworking office with a notarized lease and workplace registration may pass initial KYC but triggers higher tax inspection attention.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Physical-inspection checklist: (1) National Tax Service field inspection at Business Registration Certificate issuance; (2) municipal tax or license team verification of the office lease; (3) bank AML team site visit before opening the corporate account; (4) customs inspection if auto parts are imported or warehoused; (5) labor inspection if employees are hired; and (6) National Tax Service Hometax address verification against VAT invoices. Quantified risk for a purely online auto-parts reseller with a proper registered office and lease is 25-35% within the first 12 months; for a mailbox-only or unverifiable arrangement, the risk rises to 70-85% within the first 6 months. Shared offices with a lease and access control generally pass inspection but should be documented as the shared business address on tax invoices and bank records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Part III, Chapter V, Articles 543 through 583 (Yuhan Hoesa, a limited liability company); Articles 289, 292, 549 and 577; Commercial Registration Act, Articles 3, 12 and 19; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its delegated regulations for non-resident capital inflows.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, District Court of the Republic of Korea having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registration Division); filings may be lodged through the Korean Court-Net i-registration electronic portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Corporation Registration Application (application for commencement of commercial registration) with the notarized Articles of Incorporation (Jung-gwan), capital payment certificate, and consent forms of appointed statutory officers.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. A Yuhan Hoesa may be incorporated with any paid-in capital amount fixed in the Articles of Incorporation; no blocked escrow account is required. All issued shares must be subscribed and fully paid in on or before the date of the registration application. For non-resident shareholders, the subscription funds must be remitted through a bank authorized to handle foreign exchange and reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; a source-and-ownership statement may be required for AML review.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF KR_YUHANGHOESA (YUHAN HOESA).
The Board of Directors, having been duly constituted by the founding members of KR_YUHANGHOESA, a Yuhan Hoesa organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, convened at the registered office and unanimously adopted the following resolutions, subject to the completion of the incorporation registration.
1. Share Capital Subscription. The Board confirmed that each member has subscribed for the number of shares set out in the Articles of Incorporation and that all contributions have been fully paid in cash or non-cash property before the date of registration. The Board approved the aggregate paid-in capital of the company and directed that the capital schedule be filed with the District Court as part of the incorporation application.
2. Registered Office. The Board adopted the address stated in the Articles as the registered office of the company in the Republic of Korea. The registered office shall be the statutory seat of the company and the location for service of process and maintenance of statutory books, subject to lawful relocation by future resolution.
3. Banking Authorization. The Board authorized the Representative Director and the Treasurer Director to open and maintain corporate bank accounts, including domestic currency and foreign currency accounts, with commercial banks in the Republic of Korea, to appoint authorized signatories, to execute account agreements and electronic banking mandates, and to submit foreign exchange transaction filings to the appropriate authorities. Payments exceeding KRW 50,000,000 shall require the joint signature of the Representative Director and one other director.
4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The Board appointed the persons identified in the appointment consents to the offices of Representative Director, Director, and Auditor. Each appointed officer consented in writing to serve in accordance with the company's Articles and the Commercial Act. The Representative Director is authorized to represent the company in all ordinary business matters, and the Auditor is empowered to inspect corporate records and financial statements.
5. Delegation and Implementation. The Board delegated to the Representative Director and to any legal or accounting adviser engaged by the company the power to execute, notarize, register, and submit all documents required for incorporation, tax registration, banking activation, and online-sales reporting, and to make any administrative corrections necessary to secure the company's legal operation.
This resolution shall be incorporated into the minutes of the first board meeting and is conclusive evidence of the unanimous consent of the directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare, notarize and authenticate the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public (under the Notary Act); no prior government approval is required for the articles for a Yuhan Hoesa.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding members must prepare Korean-language Articles of Incorporation naming the corporate entity as KR_YUHANGHOESA. The articles must identify the total authorized shares and par value, each member's subscription, the exact registered office in the Republic of Korea, the business purpose of online retail of automotive replacement parts and tuning accessories, the number of directors and statutory auditor, and the fiscal year end. Each founding member or authorized attorney-in-fact must appear before a notary, verify identity, and acknowledge the document. The notary will notarize the articles. For non-resident founders with a remote execution, the local power of attorney must be apostilled or legally certified. The final notarized original must be retained for submission to the court registration.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Signature pages of all founding members
Notarized passport or foreign corporate certificate of each founder
Executed power of attorney if using a local administrative agent
Statement of subscribed share allocation and capital contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry queries the provisions, amend the offending provisions, revoke and re-notarize the revised articles, and resubmit; incomplete identification will be cured by producing original passports or apostilled company extracts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pay subscriptions and obtain a capital payment certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized foreign exchange bank in Korea (e.g., retail banking center of a commercial bank licensed by the Financial Services Commission)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the draft articles are finalized, the representative shall open a dedicated bank account using the proposed corporate name or an escrow-designated account in the incorporators' joint names and deposit the full amount of each member's subscription. The bank will verify the payment against the subscription schedule and issue a capital payment certificate acceptable to the District Court. If non-resident shareholders transfer foreign currency, the bank shall record the transaction in the Foreign Exchange Information System and issue a certificate of inward remittance. The representative shall preserve all remittance slips, bank confirmation letters, and source-of-funds documents for the court registration file and for later AML audits.
required_dossiers: Subscription schedule
Draft of notarized Articles of Incorporation
Shareholders' passports or corporate certificates for AML review
Bank new-account application forms
Statement of source of funds if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays the certificate, provide corroborative remittance slips and bank statements; if an AML query arises, submit a detailed ownership and source-of-wealth statement. For rejected foreign transfers, resubmit with the corrected remittance purpose code for investment in a domestic company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation registration with the district court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the planned registered office; e-filing through Korean Court-Net i-registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The local agent or representative director must submit to the court the notarized articles, capital payment certificate, court application form for corporation registration, written consents to appointment from each director and auditor, a copy of the lease agreement for the registered office with landlord's written consent, and evidence of payment of registration tax and local education surtax. The court will check the legal existence of all required particulars and enter the company into the commercial register. Upon approval, the court will issue the certificate of registered matters, and a standard seal certificate may be obtained after registering the corporate seal impression.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital payment certificate
Corporation registration application form
Written consent to take office signed by each director and auditor
Registered office lease contract and landlord's consent
Passports or identity documents of all directors
Receipt of registration tax and education surtax payment
Application for registration of corporate seal impression
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is suspended or rejected, inspect the court's correction instructions, remedy the indicated deficiencies such as signature notarization, lease consent, or capital certificate, and re-file within the statutory correction period without paying an additional registration fee; if the court erroneously rejects the application, an immediate objection may be raised to the court under applicable non-contentious proceedings rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax registration, local online-sales notification and corporate governance filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (district tax office with jurisdiction over registered office); local district office for online mail-order sales report; Korea Internet and Security Agency for privacy disclosure if personal information is processed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days after incorporation, the representative director must apply for the company's business registration certificate with the district tax office, attaching the certified corporate registration, lease contract, corporate seal certificate, and director identity documents. The tax office will assign a business registration number and VAT registration. Because the company operates an online sales platform for automotive parts, it must file the online communication sales business report with the relevant local district office and, if processing customer personal information, register the privacy policy and appoint a domestic privacy manager. The company must also place its e-commerce operator identification signage in the online storefront and maintain records for consumer dispute resolution. After obtaining the tax certificate, the company may complete merchant onboarding for Stripe and PayPal after their internal KYC review.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registered matters
Registered seal certificate
Copy of lease contract
Articles of Incorporation
Tax office business registration application
Online sales notification form and identity of privacy manager
Bank account certificate or foreign bank details for Stripe and PayPal settlement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office rejects or queries the business purpose, amend the Articles and resubmit the corporate detail; if the local office suspends the online sales notification, correct the business operator's identity details and obtain a new certificate on the same or next business day.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - this is a pure online retail operation under ISIC 4791 with no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing activity. If a local warehouse is later established, the competent authority would be the local municipal building and fire safety department under the Building Act and Fire Safety Act.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable; no industrial or manufacturing operating permit is required for online retail of automotive replacement parts and tuning accessories under ISIC 4791.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no EIA is required for online retail of automotive parts because there is no physical production, discharge, or waste generation activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no civil defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or workplace safety approval is required for the registered online sales office. If the company later opens a warehouse or distribution center, a fire protection certificate and industrial workplace safety inspection may be required under Korea's Fire Prevention and Safety Act and Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity that creates a Korean domestic place of business must file the corporate business registration application with the district tax office that has jurisdiction over that place of business within 20 days of business commencement, obtaining an 11-digit business registration number (TIN) which also operates as the VAT registration number. The application can be submitted through the HomeTax portal, by a certified tax agent, or at the district tax office; supporting documents include foreign incorporation/registration certificates, proof of the Korean place of business (lease agreement or office registration), the appointment of a domestic tax representative where required, and board resolution or branch head authorization. For the newly formed domestic Yuhan Hoesa (LLC), registration is performed by filing the standard Application for Business Registration together with its Korean certificate of incorporation, and the NTS issues the Business Registration Certificate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation subject to entity-level Korean corporate income tax; Korea has no check-the-box classification election. Hybrid mismatch outcomes may be adjusted through the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs but are non-elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Korea requires VAT registration from the first taxable supply for an incorporated entity, so the effective threshold is zero. For unincorporated/simplified businesses, KRW 80,000,000 annual tax-exclusive taxable turnover separates the simplified taxable person regime from the general taxpayer regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The Yuhan Hoesa must issue electronic tax invoices (e-tax invoices) for ordinary B2B supplies and transmit them to the National Tax Service through the HomeTax E-Invoice system by the statutory tax invoice deadline. The NTS provides bulk transmission APIs and EDI for high-volume taxpayers, assigns electronic numbers to received invoices, and reconciles seller/buyer filings for anti-fraud detection. There is no separate third-party pre-clearance digital stamping requirement for export-only movements, but the e-tax invoice must be linked to the export declaration to substantiate zero rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export treatment is available for goods supplied to a foreign purchaser and physically exported from Korea under a valid customs export declaration, and for exported services actually performed or used outside Korea as specified in the VAT Act Enforcement Decree. For the online automotive parts retail scope, zero rating requires that the parts leave Korea under customs supervision and that legal title and physical delivery pass to an overseas customer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Customs Declaration (Declaration of Exportation) approved through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill showing the foreign port/destination
Export sales contract / purchase order with the foreign buyer
Bank-issued Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation (or an Inward Remittance Certificate / FIRC if accepted by the relevant exchange bank) evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Korea Customs Service export clearance log/UNI-PASS printout
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service jointly verify that the export declaration, shipping documents, and foreign currency collection evidence are consistent. If the zero-rated claim is not substantiated by the required customs and FX documentation, the NTS will retroactively assess output VAT on the supply, deny or claw back any VAT refund or input tax credit, and impose additional tax penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act. Serious or fraudulent abuse can result in criminal referral, fines, and personal liability for directors and representatives.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS), and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a market-based current-account convertibility regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won is fully convertible for trade-related current transactions and ordinary service payments; residents and non-residents may freely convert through designated foreign exchange banks within reporting thresholds. Capital-account operations, however, remain regulated: foreign direct investment must be notified through the Korea Trade Investment Promotion Agency or a designated foreign exchange bank, and portfolio flows are subject to reporting and, in stress periods, prudential limits. Exporters do not face a surrender requirement; proceeds may be retained in foreign currency or converted at market rates. Profit remittance is permitted but subject to evidenced tax residency, audited financial statements, withholding tax at 20% or treaty-reduced rate, and, for dividend outflows, prior foreign exchange bank reporting. Transfer-pricing documentation may be requested under Korea's global anti-base-erosion rules. Therefore, convertibility is robust on the current account, but treasury plans must build time buffers for capital reporting, tax waivers, and beneficiary verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, export proceeds must generally be collected within three months from the date of export declaration, with extension possible up to six months or longer for deferred-payment, shipbuilding, or plant-export contracts. There is no mandatory conversion ratio in South Korea; exporters may hold 100% of export receipts in a designated foreign-currency deposit account at a foreign exchange bank. No surrender to the Bank of Korea is required. Late collection or non-collection must be reported and may trigger a foreign-exchange violation review.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW/USD)
Capital Account under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and Operational KRW Settlements Account
Foreign Currency Deposit Account and General Corporate Settlement Account
FIPA Investment Capital Account and Trade Settlement Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low and legally constrained. Offshore fintech EMIs cannot serve as the primary treasury account for a Korean-resident entity unless licensed under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and authorized by the Financial Services Commission. Non-resident digital banks such as remote EMI providers do not have the legal right to open KRW-denominated corporate accounts or issue a Korean business IBAN for the Yuhan Hoesa. PayPal and Stripe may be integrated as online acquiring rails for consumer card payments, but their settlement payouts must be swept into a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank account. For cross-border liquidity, the only compliant treasury structure is a domestic foreign-exchange bank account linked to the Foreign Exchange Information System, with outward remittances reported through the designated bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandate: High. For a Yuhan Hoesa with non-resident shareholders and directors, at least one statutory director or a duly authorized corporate representative must appear physically in-branch to execute account-opening KYC and signatory verification. Although some Korean banks offer assisted e-KYC for foreigners with apostilled documents and video interviews, remote consular proxy opening is not generally accepted. The bank will require a valid passport or Alien Registration Card, a Korean business registration certificate, an original power of attorney if a representative acts, and corporate minutes authorizing the account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or director with high-risk jurisdiction nexus and no verifiable source for the capital injection into the Korean LLC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier containing apostilled certificates of incorporation and good standing, board resolution, shareholder and UBO register, source-of-funds statement from a regulated home-country bank, twelve months of bank statements, audited or certified financial statements of the investing shareholder, personal tax clearance certificate, and if any ownership is held by a legal entity, a certified registry extract identifying all natural persons above 10%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce auto-parts inventory may contain components with dual-use or export-control sensitivity, and aggregated Stripe/PayPal consumer flows could obscure sanctioned end-users.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: HS-code classification for every product line, customs commodity list, documented export-control and sanctions-screening policy, live sanctions-screening outputs against OFAC/UN/EU/Japan/Korea lists, customer end-use attestations, logistics and freight-forwarder screening records, and if applicable, a determination or license issued through Korea's strategic trade control system.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound funds arrive from an unrelated third party or settlement flows from Stripe/PayPal do not match invoicing, raising potential concerns of money mule, invoice fraud, or attempted funding of an unregistered foreign investment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized investment agreement in the same names, routing confirmation from the remitting bank showing the Korean purpose code for foreign direct investment, Stripe/PayPal merchant settlement statements, order-level transaction logs, user refund policy, and a reconciliation working paper tying every inbound SWIFT to either share issuance or inventory sales payouts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Yuhan Hoesa uses a virtual office or single-mailbox registered address, making the bank unable to evidence operational substance for an auto-parts e-commerce business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement in the company name, utility bill matching the registered address, live e-commerce platform seller pages, warehousing and logistics contracts, staffing records, inventory purchase agreements, photo evidence of the operation, and the Korean Saeupja Deungnok business registration certificate showing a valid corporate registration number.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a compliant inbound equity injection, the non-resident investor should file a foreign investment notification through the Korea Trade Investment Promotion Agency or the designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The remittance must be sent via SWIFT MT103 from the investor's own account to the Yuhan Hoesa's foreign-currency capital escrow account. The wire must state a qualified FDI purpose code and be supported by the investment declaration, corporate flowchain pack, and purpose-of-remittance explanation. The receiving domestic bank will credit the foreign-currency deposit, issue a capital verification certificate, and permit conversion into KRW only after the entity registration and share issuance are completed. If the incoming amount is below KRW 100 million and the foreign ownership is below the statutory threshold, it is treated as a standard foreign-exchange transaction rather than FIPA-recognized foreign investment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For retail auto-parts supplier payments and wholesale battery and aftermarket-part procurement, the company should use SWIFT MT103 with the bank-applicable import/trade settlement purpose code, attaching commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, and supplier contracts. Documentary collections, including D/P and D/A, are acceptable for low-risk recurring parts purchases. Commercial letters of credit through a confirming bank are recommended for high-value bulk orders. All outbound wires must be reported through the Foreign Exchange Information System by the servicing Tier-1 bank; there are no clearing restrictions provided the beneficiary banks are in jurisdictions not subject to UN or Korean financial sanctions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/KRW forward exchange contracts maturing within 12 months and supported by committed trade invoices or cash-flow forecasts
European-style USD/KRW FX options purchased from an onshore foreign-exchange bank to cap adverse exchange-rate movements
Cross-currency swaps (USD/KRW) with genuine trade receivable, payable, or dividend exposure and zero speculative leverage

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only in limited onshore/offshore interbank cases with underlying economic exposure and regulatory reporting to the Bank of Korea, not recommended as a standard Yuhan Hoesa treasury tool

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Local Income Tax Surtax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following the fiscal year-end; extended to May 31 if financial statements are audited and the annual shareholders' meeting is held before the applicable due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% additional tax on under-reported/unfiled taxable income; 0.022% daily interest charge on unpaid taxes; administrative tax lien, asset seizure, and forced closure of business registration after prolonged delinquency (typically 2+ years); NTS may request court-ordered strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting and Approval of Statutory Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed with any government body for a private LLC; must be documented in the corporate minute book and retained at registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (for a December 31 year-end, no later than June 30); financial statements must be available for inspection for 7 years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commercial Act penalties for directors for failure to convene AGM; administrative fine of up to KRW 2 million (approx. USD 1,500); inability to use financial statements for tax and legal purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Mandatory External Audit Report Filing (if statutory thresholds are exceeded)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and National Tax Service (NTS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of fiscal year-end (April 30 for December fiscal year); may be extended to May 31 to coincide with the income tax return deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to undergo mandatory audit: fines up to KRW 50 million (approx. USD 38,000); rejection of tax-deductible expenses; administrative sanctions against directors; potential auditor designation by FSS at company expense.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registration of Changes in Shareholders, Directors, Registered Capital and Company Details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Court of Registration (Commercial Registry) at the local district court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after any change (share transfers, director changes, address changes, etc.); annual confirmation is not separately required in Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 1 million (approx. USD 750) for failure to file required changes; provisional disposition prohibiting unlawful registration; long-term non-compliance may lead to administrative strike-off by the court.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Korean private LLC is subject to mandatory external audit under the 'Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and Other Companies' if, as of the preceding fiscal year-end: (a) total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 9.2 million); or (b) annual sales revenue exceeds KRW 10 billion (approx. USD 7.7 million); or (c) total liabilities exceed KRW 7 billion (approx. USD 5.4 million). Additional triggering criteria apply if the entity is parent to a group requiring consolidated audits or if designated by the Financial Services Commission.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) for entities listed or designated by the FSS; non-listed private LLCs may apply Korean GAAP (K-GAAP)/SME Accounting Standards. All statutory audits must be performed in accordance with Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not maintain a separate annual UBO confirmation regime for private LLCs. However, actual ownership and shareholding changes must be registered with the Court of Registration within 30 days, and the internal register must be updated continuously. The company secretary shall perform an annual internal review of the UBO register, documenting any changes and notifying the NTS where requested. Directors must also confirm the accuracy of the registered capital and shareholder information in the annual tax return.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9%-24% progressive national corporate income tax, plus 10% local income tax surtax; aggregate top marginal rate is 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No e-commerce-specific tax holiday; statutory incentives are granted under the Tax Incentive Limitation Act: R&D tax credits up to 30%-40% for qualifying R&D, foreign-invested high-tech enterprises in foreign investment zones may obtain a 50% corporate tax reduction for 3-5 years, SME tax rate reductions and facility investment tax credits apply; South Korea does not maintain a patent box regime

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Return (Corporate Income Tax Act Article 60), filed electronically through the South Korean National Tax Service HomeTax portal at hometax.go.kr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; domestic corporations with prior-year national corporate tax liability exceeding KRW 10 million must also make semi-annual intermediate payments in April and October
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the filing deadline is March 31; a one-month extension may be obtained by filing an extension request through HomeTax before the original deadline

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate Identification and Fiscal Year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name, business registration number, tax office, tax classification code, fiscal year beginning and end, industry classification code attributable to online retail of automotive replacement parts and tuning accessories
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose full foreign ownership chain, non-resident shareholding percentages, ultimate parent entity, jurisdiction of tax residence, and local agent details; false declaration of ownership may invalidate treaty rate claims and trigger anti-money-laundering reporting obligations

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Financial Statements and Gross Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue derived from online sales of auto parts, cost of sales, gross profit, selling general and administrative expenses, operating income, and other income as reflected in the Korean GAAP financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All Stripe, PayPal, and bank card settlements in respect of Korean customers must be reconciled into taxable turnover; non-resident merchants using a Korean logistics warehouse may create a permanent establishment, requiring full Korean-source revenue recognition and allocation of profits to the Korean branch

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses, entertainment expenses exceeding statutory ceilings, corporate taxes, fines, donations in excess of limits, prior period adjustments, and deduction of exempt income and non-taxable items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Arm's-length transfer pricing adjustments must be recorded here; intercompany royalties, management fees, interest, and director fees paid to non-residents are deductible only if economically substantiated and after proper withholding; undocumented cross-border payments are disallowed and may be treated as constructive dividends to the non-resident parent

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying loss carryforwards, prior year deficit deductions, and tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 10-year corporate tax loss carryforward period; for a Korean corporation owned by non-residents, the ability to offset losses may be scrutinized if the losses arise from below-arm's-length imports or payments to the foreign parent; local-source ring-fencing rules apply to non-resident branches but the subject entity is a domestic Korean LLC, so worldwide income is the starting point

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Tax Calculation and Progressive Rates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of national corporate income tax using the statutory brackets: 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 21% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 10% local income tax surtax is not entered in this box but must be computed later; all tax rates apply to the foreign-owned Korean LLC in the same manner as a domestically owned LLC; no special non-resident rate is permitted for the Korean domestic entity itself

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Tax Credits and Foreign Tax Credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for foreign taxes paid on foreign-source income, R&D credits, employment creation credits, facility investment credits, and tax subsidies available under the Tax Incentive Limitation Act
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign tax credit cannot exceed the Korean corporate tax attributable to the corresponding foreign-source income; the non-resident parent's home-country taxes are not creditable in the Korean entity unless and until such taxes are borne by the Korean entity; treaty relief for outbound payments is separately processed through withholding reconciliation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory schedule disclosing all cross-border related-party transactions, including sales of auto parts, commissions, logistics fees, software subscriptions, royalties, intercompany debt interest, and payments to foreign directors
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This attachment is the statutory transfer-pricing flag; file even if no tax is due; failure to report related-party transactions may trigger separate penalties and toll the time period for transfer-pricing adjustments; identify the counterparty jurisdiction, amount, transaction code, and transfer-pricing method applied

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of Korean-source income paid to non-residents, including dividends, interest, royalties, rental income, technical service fees, and other income subject to withholding tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile every payment made to the non-resident beneficial owner and maintain the Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership form in the taxpayer file; the Korean LLC as withholding agent is primarily liable for un-withheld tax plus penalties if the reduced treaty rate is applied without documentary support

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax surtax equal to 10% of the final national corporate income tax liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The local surtax return must be filed simultaneously with the national corporate tax return; no treaty exemption applies to the Korean local income tax surtax; the non-resident parent cannot avoid the surtax by treaty since it is imposed on the Korean domestic entity's income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 - Attestation, Attachments, and Electronic Signature
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signatures of the representative director and responsible tax accountant, audited financial statements, tax adjustment schedules, and supporting documentation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A false electronic signature on the corporate income tax return constitutes fraudulent tax evasion for both the representative director and the tax accountant; if the Korean LLC is managed by a foreign director abroad, the director must appoint a domestic tax agent with a valid power of attorney before filing

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes, a late-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax applies if the return is filed within one month after the statutory deadline, increasing to 30% if filed more than one month late; the fraudulent understatement penalty is 40% of the underpaid tax; unpaid corporate tax accrues a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.022%; criminal tax evasion is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines of up to 5 times the tax evaded; a company that deliberately omits online payment rails may also face aggravated penalties and loss of tax clearance certificates

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate statutory withholding tax on outbound dividends, comprised of 20% national corporate income tax withholding plus 2% local income tax surtax
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the home-country tax authority and a beneficial ownership declaration to the Korean withholding agent before the payment date; the Korean agent must file the treaty relief application with the National Tax Service through HomeTax, retain the TRC, ownership documents, and underlying payment contracts for at least 5 years, and if treaty reduction is not applied at source, the non-resident may file a timely refund claim against the NTS within the statutory five-year period
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding on cross-border royalties and interest is 22% aggregate (20% national plus 2% local); under Korea's bilateral tax treaties the reduced rates vary by counterparty, with interest commonly reduced to 10% and royalties reduced to 10%-15%, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and has no permanent establishment in Korea to which the income is effectively connected

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5,000,000,000 aggregate cross-border related-party transactions in a fiscal year triggers mandatory Local File and related disclosure; Master File and Country-by-Country Report are triggered for multinational groups with consolidated global revenue of at least KRW 1,000,000,000,000
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not administer a standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime like the UAE; however, the National Tax Service applies the OECD core income-generating activities analysis in determining treaty entitlement, beneficial ownership, permanent establishment presence, and anti-abuse recharacterization; a Korean LLC lacking real office, employees, business decisions, and operational control over auto-parts e-commerce activities may be denied DTA benefits as a mere shell or conduit, with the NTS recharacterizing the transactions under the substance-over-form principle and the Framework Act on International Tax Adjustment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating online auto-parts sales revenue, depositing Stripe and PayPal settlements into undisclosed foreign bank accounts, creating fabricated purchase invoices for Chinese or Korean suppliers, and overstating inventory costs to depress the Korean corporate tax base
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act imposes imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to 5 times the evaded tax; the Framework Act on National Taxes imposes a 40% fraudulent understatement penalty plus a 0.022% daily late-payment surcharge on the unpaid corporate tax; the NTS may simultaneously assess additional corporate tax, local income tax, value-added tax, and all related penalties, and may publish the taxpayer and director as habitual tax evaders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the National Tax Collection Act, a director who willfully or grossly negligently fails to collect or pay corporate taxes is personally and jointly liable to satisfy the unpaid corporate tax from personal assets; the director may face overseas travel restrictions and immigration blacklisting for tax arrears exceeding KRW 500 million, and if the evasion scheme is proved, imprisonment of up to 5 years through criminal prosecution

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Shopping and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing a Korean paper LLC with no physical office, employees, purchase management, customer service, or decision-making functions into the ownership chain of an auto-parts e-commerce business solely to claim Korean DTA reductions on outbound royalties, interest, and dividends, or to shift profits away from the ultimate foreign beneficial owners
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Framework Act on International Tax Adjustment authorizes the NTS to deny tax treaty benefits where the principal purpose of an arrangement is treaty shopping; the NTS may recharacterize the Korean LLC as a direct taxable presence of the foreign parent, disallow the reduced treaty rate, impose the full 22% withholding together with a 40% understatement penalty and interest, and apply domestic anti-abuse rules under the general substance-over-form doctrine
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false beneficial ownership certificates or tax residency statements in support of treaty shopping are exposed to joint personal liability for the shortfall, plus monetary penalties; criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may result in imprisonment of up to 5 years; a director who is also the architect of the shell chain may face civil damages, asset seizure, and travel blacklisting pending tax collection

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Unreported Foreign Financial Accounts and Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Stripe, PayPal, and overseas bank accounts to collect Korean auto-parts retail revenue without reporting the foreign financial accounts to the Korean tax authority, failing to disclose the foreign account balance exceeding KRW 500 million at month-end, and using nominee or shadow accounts to conceal the true beneficial owner of e-commerce receipts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Information and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, failure to report foreign financial accounts may result in penalties of up to 20% of the unreported balance for severe infractions, criminal fines, and imprisonment of up to 3 years; the unreported funds are also subject to full Korean corporate income tax, value-added tax, 40% fraudulent understatement penalty, and daily delinquency charges; financial institutions are obligated to report suspicious transactions, and Stripe/PayPal merchant records are routinely demanded through tax information exchange requests
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who controls, benefits from, or orders the concealment of foreign payment accounts is personally liable for the civil restitution of unpaid taxes and penalties; the NTS and prosecution may request departure prohibitions, freeze director and shareholder assets, and obtain extradition in international mutual legal assistance; upon conviction, the director faces imprisonment of up to 3 years for AML non-compliance and up to 5 years for tax evasion, with the corporate veil pierced to the extent of personal benefit received from the concealed payment flows
